# PRD

- **Spec:** `28_ollama_provider` (id `28`, name `ollama_provider`)
- **Title:** Ollama provider on the native /api/chat API
- **Status:** active
- **Schema version:** 3
- **Created:** 2026-10-21T10:51:32.122926Z
- **Source:** docs/prd/14-run-the-agent-on-anthropic-openrouter-or-ollama.md
- **Intent hash:** `332871ef540aa3dfdf98e538628ed1fe065fc43fb6a6a0ab2c47051d5dbe0ab5`

## Intent

An AgentKit agent can run on a model served by a local or self-hosted Ollama server. It reaches the server through Ollama's own Go package, `github.com/ollama/ollama/api`, and Ollama's native `/api/chat` endpoint. This spec delivers `provider/ollama`, a `core.ProviderClient` that does three things:

- turns a canonical request into an Ollama chat request;
- streams the response back as canonical events and an assistant message;
- handles Ollama's context window, thinking, tool calls, errors and usage the way Ollama documents them.

It also adds the Ollama package as an approved, pinned dependency. Choosing this provider from `agentkit.Config` is not part of this spec.

## Goals

1. **A two-turn tool loop completes against a local recording server.**
   - Setup: the provider is `ollama.New(m, ollama.Options{Env: {"OLLAMA_HOST": <server>}})`, where `m` is the row `catalog.Select("ollama", "STANDARD", "")` returns (`qwen3.8:27b`, 32,768 / 32,768, effort `medium`). The loop is a tool call, its result, then a final text.
   - Both recorded requests carry:
     - `model` `qwen3.8:27b`;
     - `options.num_ctx` 32768;
     - `truncate: false`;
     - `think: "medium"`;
     - `stream: true`;
     - the tools, with their schemas cut to what Ollama's tool type carries.
   - The second request also carries:
     - the first turn's tool-call id;
     - its arguments with their keys in the order the server sent them;
     - the result paired to that id, with the tool's name;
     - the first turn's thinking text on the assistant message.
2. **Usage is netted and priced at zero.** A final chunk reporting `prompt_eval_count` 354, `prompt_eval_cached_count` 256 and `eval_count` 120 becomes `core.Usage{InputTokens: 98, CacheReadTokens: 256, OutputTokens: 120, Requests: 1, CostUSD: 0}`, with the cost's presence bit set.
3. **Failures are named.**
   - A stream that ends without `done: true` ends the turn with `ollama.ErrStreamTruncated`, and its message carries no tool call.
   - A 404 ends it with `ollama.ErrModelNotFound`, naming the model and `ollama pull <model>`.
   - A refused connection ends it with `ollama.ErrUnreachable`, naming the host and `ollama serve`.
4. **No other provider's settings and no credential are used.**
   - The provider reads no variable except `OLLAMA_HOST`.
   - No recorded request carries an `Authorization` header. This holds even when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OLLAMA_API_KEY` are set.
   - No other provider's value appears anywhere in a request.
5. **The dependency is approved and documented, and nothing else changes.**
   - `github.com/ollama/ollama` is a direct, approved requirement pinned at `v0.40.7`, with a ruling in `docs/DEPS.md`.
   - Every existing Anthropic and `provider/faux` test passes unchanged, and `make check` passes.

## Non-goals

These belong to other specs of this split:

- **`provider_selection`**:
  - choosing `ollama` from `agentkit.Config`;
  - building this provider inside `agentkit.New` or an exported resolution;
  - reporting the resolved provider, model and effort;
  - run-level "unpriced" flagging.
- **`provider_conformance`**:
  - the cross-provider conformance suite;
  - the opt-in live smoke test against a real Ollama server;
  - the examples' `AGENTKIT_*` variables and the README quick start.
- **`openrouter_provider`**: anything OpenRouter.

Out of scope altogether:

- Ollama's OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` or Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoints. Only native `/api/chat` is used.
- Ollama's hosted service (`https://ollama.com`, `OLLAMA_API_KEY`). It is refused (see Requirement 1).
- Managing Ollama: starting the server, pulling models, `keep_alive`, memory settings.
- Discovering limits from `/api/show`. Asking the server what length a model is loaded at.
- Retries. Explicit prompt-cache control.
- Images, audio, files and structured output (`format`).
- Parsing `<think>` tags out of visible content. Thinking is what Ollama reports in `message.thinking`.
- A request hook (`OnPayload`), custom headers, and a per-request timeout option.
- An effort clamping ladder.

## Background

**Ollama was here before.** Until PRD 10, AgentKit had a hand-written `provider/ollama` (an NDJSON wire read through `wire.NewNDJSON`). PRD 10 deleted it with the other non-Anthropic wires, because nothing used it. Traces remain:

- `core.APIOllamaChat` (`"ollama-chat"`) in `core/stopreason.go`;
- `provider.ToolResultText` (`provider/toolresult.go`), whose doc names "the rule the Ollama adapter applies";
- `docs/archive/wires.md` § "Ollama native", which says:
  - failure arrives as an error string inside a 200;
  - `OLLAMA_HOST` without a scheme needs `http://`;
  - a stream without `done: true` is truncated, not complete;
  - native thinking without a signature must not be demoted to text by repair.

The archive also records that Ollama's tool messages once paired by position with no id. The 2026-10-21 probe of `api` v0.40.7 (PRD 14) found tool calls carrying ids and results pairing by them. PRD 09 recorded that `ollama/api` fails on stream lines over about 512 KB.

**What exists to build on.**

- `provider/anthropic` is the template:
  - `Options` with `Env` and `Getenv`;
  - environment lookup in `providerEnv.Lookup` (`client.go`);
  - `Stream` refusing an already-done context, then `core.StreamChannel`;
  - a decode state with `emitStart`, `finish` (block-end events in block order, then `MessageEndEvent`) and `fail`. In `fail`, an abort gives `StopReasonAborted` and `core.ErrAborted` with no `ErrorEvent`. Anything else gives `StopReasonError`, a terminal `ErrorEvent`, then the message end;
  - `applyThinking`, which reads `core.Model.Efforts`.
- Spec 26 (`26_provider_catalog_tiers`) gives the `ollama` catalog row (`qwen3.8:27b`, 32,768 / 32,768, zero price, efforts `low`/`medium`/`high`/`max`), the fallback constants `catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow` and `catalog.OllamaDefaultMaxTokens` (32,768 each), and `catalog.Select`.
- Spec 27 (`openrouter_provider`) adds the second vendor-SDK provider, a provider-neutral tool-pairing repair in package `provider`, and the first round of policy-test edits for a new provider SDK.

**What Ollama does (the probe, 2026-10-21, `qwen3.8:27b` on a 32 GB Apple M4).**

- The loop completes at think levels low, medium, high and max. `max` is accepted silently.
- `done_reason` is `"stop"` on a turn that ends in a tool call.
- `prompt_eval_count` includes `prompt_eval_cached_count`.
- The tool schema type is a subset of JSON Schema: `additionalProperties`, `format` and bounds are dropped.
- The server ran the model at 32,768 tokens, its GPU-memory-sized default, although `/api/show` reported 262,144. `num_ctx` takes effect only when a model loads. A different value for an already-loaded model is silently ignored.

## Requirements

### 1. Construction, host and isolation

**Constructor.**
- `ollama.New(m core.Model, opts Options) (*Client, error)` builds the provider for one model. `*Client` implements `core.ProviderClient` and is safe for concurrent `Stream` calls.
- `(*Client).Host() string` returns the resolved base URL.
- `New` makes no network request.
- `New` fails when `m.ID` is empty after trimming.

**`Options` fields.**
- `Host` overrides `OLLAMA_HOST`.
- `Env` (map) and `Getenv` (func) control how variables are read; see below.
- `HTTPClient` is the `*http.Client` requests go through. Nil means a fresh client with the default transport.
- `Now` is the clock for message timestamps.
- `Warnf` receives the transcript-repair report. Nil discards it.

**Reading `OLLAMA_HOST`.**
- `Options.Host` is used when set. Otherwise `OLLAMA_HOST` is looked up the way `provider/anthropic` does it:
  1. `Options.Env` first, where an empty value falls through;
  2. then `Options.Getenv` when it is non-nil;
  3. otherwise the process environment.
- Empty or unset means `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (`ollama.DefaultHost`). The variable name is the exported constant `ollama.HostVar`.
- No other variable is read, and none at all when `Options.Host` is set.

**Parsing the host.** The value is trimmed and parsed by the rules Ollama's own CLI applies, so one value means the same server for `ollama` and for AgentKit:
- no scheme means `http` and default port 11434;
- `http://` without a port means port 80;
- `https://` without a port means port 443;
- a path is kept.

**Invalid hosts.** `New` fails with an error wrapping `ollama.ErrInvalidHost` when:
- the scheme is not `http` or `https`;
- the value cannot be parsed;
- the port is out of range;
- the host carries user information. The message shows the host with the password redacted;
- the host is `ollama.com` or a subdomain of it. The message says the hosted service is not supported.

**No credential.** The provider sends no credential.
- Its HTTP client wraps the transport in a layer that deletes any `Authorization` header before the request goes on. This covers anything the SDK might add.
- An embedder's own `HTTPClient.Transport` runs beneath that layer and may add headers of its own.

### 2. Request encoding

Each `Stream` call sends one request through the SDK client's `Chat` method, with `stream: true`.

- `model` is `m.ID`, exactly as written.
- **Messages, in order:**
  - one `system` message whose content is the text blocks of `Request.System` joined by a blank line, omitted when empty;
  - then `Request.Prefix`;
  - then the repaired `Request.Messages` (Requirement 4).
- **`options.num_ctx`** is sent on every request: `m.ContextWindow`, or `catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow` when that is not positive.
- **`truncate: false`** is sent on every request.
- **`options.num_predict`:**
  - the requested `MaxTokens` when it is positive and not above `m.MaxOutputTokens`;
  - otherwise `m.MaxOutputTokens` when that is positive;
  - otherwise the requested value when it is positive;
  - otherwise nothing.
- **Sampling.** `options.temperature`, `options.top_p` and `options.stop` are sent when set on the request. An explicit temperature of 0 is sent.
- `keep_alive`, `format` and images are never sent.

### 3. Tools and tool choice

- Each `core.ToolWire` is declared as a function tool with its name, its description, and the part of its input schema that Ollama's tool-parameter type carries. The provider produces that part by encoding the full schema as JSON and decoding it into the SDK's parameter type, so whatever the type does not model is dropped (`additionalProperties`, `format`, bounds).
- A tool with no schema is declared as an empty object schema (`{"type":"object","properties":{}}`).
- Tools keep their request order.
- A schema the SDK type cannot decode fails the turn before any request is sent, with an error naming the tool.
- **Tool choice.** Unset or `auto` sends the tools. `none` sends no `tools` key at all, because Ollama has no tool choice.
- Arguments are still validated against the full schema before any tool runs. This is existing loop behaviour and needs no new code here.

### 4. Replaying the transcript

- Before encoding, `Request.Messages` goes through the provider-neutral tool-pairing repair that `openrouter_provider` adds to package `provider`. It does three things:
  - drops failed or aborted assistant turns;
  - drops results orphaned by them;
  - adds a synthetic "No result provided" result for an unanswered call, in call order.

  When the repair changed anything, its report goes to `Warnf`. The input slice is never mutated.
- **A user message** is sent as role `user`, with its text as content.
- **An assistant message** is sent as role `assistant`:
  - `content` is its text;
  - `thinking` is the concatenated text of its thinking blocks, but only when the message's `Model` equals `m.ID` and the block is not redacted. Other thinking is dropped and never sent as content;
  - `tool_calls` lists one entry per `ToolUseBlock`, with the block's id, its position as index, its name, and arguments decoded from `ToolUseBlock.Input` with the key order of those bytes kept.
- **A tool result** is one `tool` message per result, in transcript order:
  - content is `provider.ToolResultText` (an error result is prefixed `Error: `);
  - the tool's name;
  - the tool-call id it answers.

### 5. Effort

The effort becomes Ollama's `think` value. The catalog row is read the same way `provider/anthropic` reads it:

- an empty effort sends no `think`;
- a model whose `ThinkingKind` is `none` sends no `think`;
- a nil `Efforts` map sends the effort by its own name;
- with a map, an effort that is absent or nil sends nothing, and a listed effort sends its value, trimmed and lower-cased, as a string level.

So `xhigh` on the `qwen3.8:27b` row sends no `think`, and `high` on an unlisted model sends `"high"`. Nothing is clamped to another level.

### 6. Streaming decode

**Message start.** On the first chunk the provider pushes `MessageStartEvent`. The partial message holds `Model` = `m.ID`, `Effort` = the request's effort, and `Timestamp` from `Options.Now`.

**Text and thinking.**
- Non-empty `message.thinking` is streamed as thinking events (`ThinkingStartEvent`, `ThinkingDeltaEvent`). Non-empty `message.content` is streamed as text events.
- A switch between kinds closes the open block. Each completed block is appended to the partial message, followed by a `MessageUpdateEvent`.
- Reasoning is never reported as visible text.

**Tool calls.** Each tool call in a chunk becomes one `ToolUseBlock`:
- the vendor's id is kept;
- a call with no id gets a synthesized id that is unique within the response and across responses;
- `Input` is the arguments' JSON, with keys in wire order. It goes through `core.NewToolUse`, so absent arguments become `{}`;
- events: `ToolCallStartEvent`, then one `ToolInputDeltaEvent` carrying the whole argument JSON. The block is then appended.

**The final chunk.** On the chunk with `done: true`, after its own content is processed:
1. Block-end events (`TextEndEvent`, `ThinkingEndEvent`, `ToolCallEndEvent`) are pushed in block order.
2. The final message is built:
   - `StopReason`: `done_reason` `length` gives `StopReasonLength`. Otherwise a message with tool calls gives `StopReasonToolUse`. Otherwise `StopReasonStop`;
   - `RawStopReason` is `done_reason` verbatim;
   - `ResponseModel` is the chunk's model;
   - `Usage` follows Requirement 9.
3. `MessageEndEvent` is pushed and the stream ends.

### 7. Incomplete turns

- **Context already done.** `Stream` returns the context's error and no channel. Every later failure is carried in the stream: the failed message, then `Err` on the last item.
- **Truncated stream.** A stream that ends, or whose SDK call returns, without a `done: true` chunk ends the turn with `ErrStreamTruncated`:
  - `StopReasonError` and a terminal `ErrorEvent`;
  - the message keeps the text and thinking that streamed and carries no tool call.
- **Cancellation.** Cancelling the caller's context stops the request promptly. The turn ends with:
  - `StopReasonAborted`;
  - `ErrorMessage` "Request was aborted", the text `provider/anthropic` and `provider/faux` use;
  - `Err` = `core.ErrAborted`;
  - no `ErrorEvent`, and no tool call in the message.

### 8. Errors

Every error text starts with `ollama:`. Cancellation (Requirement 7) takes precedence over every case below.

- **Unreachable host.** A failure to connect (refused, DNS, no route) wraps `ErrUnreachable`. The text names the host, suggests `ollama serve`, and names `OLLAMA_HOST`.
- **Model not pulled.** A 404 wraps `ErrModelNotFound` and is also a `*ollama.StatusError` with `Code` 404. The text names the model and the host, includes Ollama's message, and suggests `ollama pull <model>`.
- **Context window.** An error whose Ollama message says the input exceeds the context length wraps `ErrContextWindow`. The text names the model and the `num_ctx` sent, includes Ollama's message, and says that a model already loaded at a smaller length keeps it until it unloads. This can arrive as a status error or as an in-stream error.
- **401 or 403.** A `*StatusError` whose text names the host, says AgentKit sends no credential to Ollama, and says to check `OLLAMA_HOST`.
- **Any other non-2xx.** A `*StatusError{Code, Text}` with the text `ollama: HTTP <code>: <Ollama's message>`.
- **An error line inside a 200 stream** ends the turn with Ollama's message, classified by the same rules.
- **No retries.** There is exactly one HTTP attempt per `Stream` call.
- No error text, event or warning contains the value of any environment variable other than the host.

### 9. Usage and cost

These come from the `done: true` chunk.

- `InputTokens` is `prompt_eval_count − prompt_eval_cached_count`, floored at 0.
- `CacheReadTokens` is the cached count, set only when it is positive.
- `OutputTokens` is `eval_count`.
- Reasoning tokens are not reported by Ollama and are not set.
- `Requests` is 1 on every turn, failed turns included.
- **Cost.** Whenever the done chunk reported usage, the cost is set to 0 with its presence bit. Ollama runs on the embedder's hardware, so a run on Ollama is priced at zero, not unpriced. This holds for listed and unlisted ids alike.
- A turn that failed before its done chunk carries no token fields.

## Design Decisions

1. **Requests go through the SDK's `api.Client.Chat`, built with `api.NewClient(base, httpClient)`, never `api.ClientFromEnvironment`.** The input requires Ollama's own package. `ClientFromEnvironment` reads the process environment through `envconfig`, which bypasses `Options.Env` and `Getenv` and breaks test isolation.
2. **Responses are decoded from the SDK's typed `ChatResponse`, not from raw NDJSON, so there is no `wire.Guard` and no bounded frame reader.** The SDK does not expose the bytes. Argument key order relies on the SDK's argument type keeping insertion order, and `Input` is its JSON encoding. Number literals may be re-rendered, which the input accepts by asking only for key order.
3. **`New` returns `(*Client, error)` and fails only for an empty model id or an invalid host.** This mirrors `openrouter.New`. Failing at construction surfaces a bad `OLLAMA_HOST` before any run.
4. **`OLLAMA_HOST` is parsed by Ollama's CLI rules (default port 11434 without a scheme; 80 or 443 with one), reimplemented here.** One value must mean the same server for `ollama` and for AgentKit, and `envconfig.Host()` cannot be pointed at `Options.Env`.
5. **A host on `ollama.com`, or one carrying user information, is refused.** The hosted service is a non-goal. User information in a URL is a credential that Go's HTTP client would send as basic auth, against the "no credential is read or sent" rule.
6. **The transport layer deletes `Authorization` beneath the SDK and above the embedder's transport.** It enforces "no credential sent" whatever the SDK does internally, and still lets an embedder that fronts Ollama with an auth proxy add a header deliberately.
7. **`Options.Host` overrides `OLLAMA_HOST`.** It gives tests and `provider_selection` an explicit endpoint, like `anthropic.Options.BaseURL`.
8. **`num_ctx` is sent on every request. A model with no window gets `catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow`, so `provider/ollama` imports `catalog`.** The window the agent prunes against must be the one the model loads at. Spec 26 says no Ollama limit is written in Go outside `catalog`.
9. **`num_predict` follows the Anthropic `max_tokens` rule (the requested value when positive and within the cap, else the cap).** It is the same contract for `Request.MaxTokens` on every provider.
10. **The tool schema is cut down by encoding it and decoding it into the SDK's parameter type.** "The part of the schema its API carries" is then exactly what the pinned SDK models, and that grows with the SDK without code here.
11. **Tool choice `none` sends no tools.** Ollama has no tool-choice field (input §5).
12. **The transcript repair is `openrouter_provider`'s provider-neutral one. Thinking is replayed only on unredacted blocks from turns of the same model.** One repair serves both new providers. Thinking from another vendor or model is meaningless or opaque to Ollama, and turning it into text would re-send it as visible content (`wires.md`).
13. **A tool call with no id gets a synthesized id that is unique within and across responses.** The loop needs a unique id per call, and `wires.md` records that per-response scoping prevents collisions. Results are also sent with the tool's name, so a server that pairs by name or position still lines them up.
14. **`done_reason` `length` maps to `StopReasonLength` even when there are tool calls. Otherwise tool calls map to `StopReasonToolUse`, and otherwise the result is `StopReasonStop`.** The loop already refuses to run calls from a length-truncated turn. The probe shows `stop` accompanying tool calls.
15. **A truncated or aborted turn's message carries no tool call.** It matches `openrouter_provider`, so the later conformance suite asserts one behaviour, and a partial call can never be executed.
16. **No retries.** A local server's failures (not running, model not pulled, out of memory, over-long input) are not transient, and the input specifies retries for OpenRouter only.
17. **404 means model not pulled. A context-window error is recognised by its message saying the input exceeds the context length. A dial failure means unreachable.** These are the three failures the input asks to explain. Each keeps Ollama's own message, so an error that is misclassified still shows what Ollama said.
18. **Cost is set to 0 with its presence bit whenever usage is reported.** The input says Ollama cost is zero. A zero that is reported keeps the agent from re-pricing it and keeps the run from being flagged unpriced.
19. **`CacheReadTokens` is set only when positive, and reasoning tokens are never set.** The SDK's integer fields cannot tell an absent count from zero, and Ollama reports no reasoning count.
20. **The SDK module is pinned at `v0.40.7`.** That is the version probed with tool-call ids and `prompt_eval_cached_count`. An upgrade is a deliberate change.
21. **The package lives in the root module (input DD2). Version moves caused by minimum version selection are recorded as accepted upgrades, and tests are restated, not deleted.** This follows the precedent of spec 14's `d1Upgrades`.
22. **`ollama.API` is `core.APIOllamaChat`.** The constant already exists, and spec 26 gives the catalog vendor the same `ollama-chat` string.

## Verified External API

The module cache is outside the repository, so none of these signatures could be read. All are **unverified**. They come from the input's probe of `api` v0.40.7 and from the package's long-standing public shape. The implementer confirms each with `go doc github.com/ollama/ollama/api` before relying on it.

| Symbol | Assumed signature / shape | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `api.NewClient` | `func NewClient(base *url.URL, http *http.Client) *Client` | unverified |
| `(*api.Client).Chat` | `func (c *Client) Chat(ctx context.Context, req *ChatRequest, fn ChatResponseFunc) error`. Calls `fn` once per streamed line. Returns nil at end of body even without `done: true`. Returns `api.StatusError` for a status ≥ 400. Returns a plain error carrying the message for an `{"error": …}` line inside a 200. | unverified |
| `api.ChatResponseFunc` | `type ChatResponseFunc func(ChatResponse) error` | unverified |
| `api.ChatRequest` | `Model string; Messages []Message; Stream *bool; Tools Tools; Options map[string]any; Think *ThinkValue; Truncate *bool` (`Truncate` per the probe) | unverified |
| `api.ThinkValue` | `struct{ Value any }`, marshalled as a bool or a string level | unverified |
| `api.Message` | `Role, Content, Thinking string; ToolCalls []ToolCall; ToolName string; ToolCallID string` (`ToolCallID` per the probe) | unverified |
| `api.ToolCall` / `api.ToolCallFunction` | `ToolCall{ID string; Function ToolCallFunction}`; `ToolCallFunction{Index int; Name string; Arguments ToolCallFunctionArguments}` | unverified |
| `api.ToolCallFunctionArguments` | Keeps insertion order through `UnmarshalJSON` / `MarshalJSON` (an ordered map) | unverified; Design Decision 2 depends on it |
| `api.Tool`, `api.Tools`, `api.ToolFunction`, `api.ToolFunctionParameters` | `Tool{Type string; Function ToolFunction}`; `ToolFunction{Name, Description string; Parameters ToolFunctionParameters}`; parameters decodable from JSON Schema, keeping type, description, enum, items, properties and required | unverified |
| `api.ChatResponse` / `api.Metrics` | `ChatResponse{Model string; Message Message; Done bool; DoneReason string; Metrics}`; `Metrics{PromptEvalCount, PromptEvalCachedCount, EvalCount int; …}` (`PromptEvalCachedCount` per the probe) | unverified |
| `api.StatusError` | `struct{ StatusCode int; Status string; ErrorMessage string }` with `Error() string` | unverified |
| `api.ClientFromEnvironment`, `envconfig.Host` | Exist and read `OLLAMA_HOST` from the process environment | unverified; deliberately not used |

## Glossary

- **OLLAMA_HOST**: The only environment variable the provider reads (ollama.HostVar); the base URL of the Ollama server, defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:11434 (ollama.DefaultHost).
- **done chunk**: The streamed /api/chat line with done:true; it carries done_reason, the response model and the token counts. A stream without it is truncated.
- **num_ctx**: Ollama's context-length option; it takes effect only when a model loads, so a model already loaded at another length keeps that length until it unloads.
- **presence bit**: The core.Usage flag recording that a field was reported, so a reported zero cost is not re-priced by Agent.priced.
- **tool-pairing repair**: provider.RepairToolPairing, added by spec 27: drops failed or aborted assistant turns and their orphaned results and inserts a synthetic "No result provided" result for each unanswered call.
- **tool-schema subset**: The part of a tool's JSON Schema that the SDK's tool-parameter type models, obtained by JSON-encoding the full schema and decoding it into that type; additionalProperties, format and bounds are dropped.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Construction, host resolution and credential isolation

**Rationale:** One OLLAMA_HOST value must mean the same server for the ollama CLI and AgentKit, and no credential may leave the process.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN ollama.New is called with a core.Model whose trimmed ID is non-empty and a valid host, THE ollama provider SHALL return a *Client that implements core.ProviderClient, make no network request, and expose the resolved base URL through (*Client).Host(); the exported constant ollama.API equals core.APIOllamaChat
   → (*Client, nil); the recording server sees zero requests after New returns; Host() returns e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
   Check: unit
   - setup: an httptest recording server counting requests
   - setup: a core.Model with ID "qwen3.8:27b"
   ```
   c, err := ollama.New(m, opts); var _ core.ProviderClient = c; assert err == nil; assert c.Host() == srv.URL; assert srv.count == 0; assert ollama.API == core.APIOllamaChat
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF ollama.New is called with a core.Model whose ID is empty after trimming whitespace, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL refuse to build the client
   → (nil, non-nil error) whose text starts with "ollama:"
   Check: unit
   - setup: a core.Model whose ID is "" and another whose ID is "   \t"
   ```
   for id in ['', '   \t']: c, err := New(Model{ID:id}, Options{}); assert c == nil; assert err != nil; assert hasPrefix(err.Error(), 'ollama:')
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE ollama provider SHALL take the host from Options.Host when it is set and read no variable at all; otherwise look up OLLAMA_HOST in Options.Env first (an empty value falls through), then through Options.Getenv when it is non-nil, otherwise from the process environment, using http://127.0.0.1:11434 (ollama.DefaultHost) when the value is empty or unset, and never read any variable other than OLLAMA_HOST
   → a Getenv spy records only the key "OLLAMA_HOST", and records nothing when Options.Host is set
   Check: unit
   - setup: a Getenv spy that records every key asked
   - setup: t.Setenv sets OLLAMA_HOST in the process environment for one case
   ```
   New(m, {Host:'h1', Getenv:spy}); assert spy.keys == []; New(m, {Env:{OLLAMA_HOST:''}, Getenv:spy}); assert spy.keys == ['OLLAMA_HOST']; assert Host()==DefaultHost when all empty
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE ollama provider SHALL for any trimmed host value, resolve the base URL by Ollama's CLI rules: no scheme means http with port 11434, http:// without a port means port 80, https:// without a port means port 443, and a path is kept
   → Host() returns e.g. "http://example.local:11434" for "example.local", "https://h:443" for "https://h", "http://h:80/proxy" for "http://h/proxy"
   Check: property
   - setup: hosts generated from scheme (none, http, https), hostname, optional port, optional path, optional surrounding whitespace
   - setup: no network
   ```
   for h in gen_hosts(): c = New(m,{Host:h}); u = parse(c.Host()); assert u.scheme == expectScheme(h); assert u.port == expectPort(h); assert u.path == pathOf(h)
   table-driven assert New(m,{Host:in}).Host() == want
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF the host value has a scheme other than http or https, cannot be parsed, or carries a port outside 1-65535, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL refuse to build the client
   → (nil, error) with errors.Is(err, ollama.ErrInvalidHost) true and text starting with "ollama:"
   Check: unit
   - setup: hosts "ftp://h", "http://[::1", "h:0", "h:65536", "http://h:99999"
   ```
   for h in bad: c, err := New(m,{Host:h}); assert c==nil; assert errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidHost); assert hasPrefix(err.Error(),'ollama:')
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF the host value carries user information, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL refuse to build the client and show the host with any password redacted
   → (nil, error) wrapping ollama.ErrInvalidHost; the error text does not contain the password
   Check: unit
   - setup: host "http://user:s3cretpw@h:11434" and "http://user@h"
   ```
   c, err := New(m,{Host:'http://user:s3cretpw@h'}); assert errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidHost); assert !contains(err.Error(),'s3cretpw')
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] IF the host is ollama.com or any subdomain of ollama.com, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL refuse to build the client and say the hosted Ollama service is not supported
   → (nil, error) wrapping ollama.ErrInvalidHost whose text says the hosted service is not supported
   Check: unit
   - setup: hosts "ollama.com", "https://ollama.com", "https://api.ollama.com:443", and "notollama.com" as a control
   ```
   for h in hosted: assert errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidHost) && contains(err.Error(),'not supported'); assert New(m,{Host:'notollama.com'}) ok
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] THE ollama provider SHALL send every request through a transport layer that deletes any Authorization header before handing the request to Options.HTTPClient's transport (or the default transport when HTTPClient is nil), so no credential is sent even when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY or OLLAMA_API_KEY are set, while an embedder's own transport beneath the layer may still add headers
   → the recording server sees no Authorization header and no other provider's variable value anywhere in any request; a header set by the embedder's RoundTripper reaches the server
   Check: integration
   - setup: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OLLAMA_API_KEY set via t.Setenv to distinctive values
   - setup: an HTTPClient whose RoundTripper adds X-Embedder: yes and also Authorization: Bearer x before delegating
   - setup: a recording httptest server
   ```
   drain(c.Stream(ctx, req)); for r in srv.requests: assert r.Header.Get('Authorization')==''; assert r.Header['X-Embedder']==['yes']; assert !containsAny(r.raw, secrets)
   ```

### REQ-2: Request encoding

**Rationale:** The window the agent prunes against must be the one the model loads at, and Request fields must mean the same thing on every provider.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN Stream is called with a live context, THE ollama provider SHALL send exactly one chat request through the SDK client's Chat method to the resolved host's /api/chat with stream true, model equal to m.ID exactly as written, truncate false, and options.num_ctx equal to m.ContextWindow
   → the recorded body carries "model", "stream":true, "truncate":false and "options":{"num_ctx":<window>,...}
   Check: integration
   - setup: a recording server
   - setup: a model with ID "Qwen3.8:27B-Odd" and ContextWindow 16384
   ```
   r = srv.only(); assert r.path=='/api/chat'; b=json(r.body); assert b.model==m.ID && b.stream==true && b.truncate==false && b.options.num_ctx==16384
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN Stream is called and m.ContextWindow is zero or negative, THE ollama provider SHALL send options.num_ctx equal to catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow
   → the recorded body carries "num_ctx":32768
   Check: unit
   - setup: models with ContextWindow 0 and -5
   - setup: catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow is 32768
   ```
   for w in [0,-5]: body = record(Model{ContextWindow:w}); assert body.options.num_ctx == catalog.OllamaDefaultContextWindow
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE ollama provider SHALL order the request messages as one system message whose content is the text blocks of Request.System joined by a blank line (omitted when that text is empty), then Request.Prefix, then the repaired Request.Messages
   → recorded messages[0] has role "system" only when Request.System has text
   Check: unit
   - setup: Request.System with two text blocks "A" and "B"
   - setup: a one-message Prefix and a one-message transcript
   - setup: a second request with no System text
   ```
   assert roles(b1.messages)==['system','user','user']; assert b1.messages[0].content=='A\n\nB'; assert 'system' not in roles(b2.messages)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE ollama provider SHALL set options.num_predict to the requested MaxTokens when it is positive and not above m.MaxOutputTokens, otherwise to m.MaxOutputTokens when that is positive, otherwise to the requested value when it is positive, and otherwise omit num_predict
   → e.g. requested 1000 with cap 32768 sends 1000; requested 50000 with cap 32768 sends 32768; no request and no cap sends no num_predict key
   Check: unit
   - setup: table: (requested 1000, cap 32768), (50000, 32768), (nil, 32768), (1000, 0), (nil, 0), (0, 0)
   ```
   for (req,cap,want) in table: b=record(); assert b.options.get('num_predict')==want
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] THE ollama provider SHALL send options.temperature, options.top_p and options.stop only when the request sets them, sending an explicit temperature of 0, and never send keep_alive, format or images
   → a request with Temperature 0 records "temperature":0; a request without sampling fields records none of those keys; no recorded body carries keep_alive, format or images
   Check: unit
   - setup: one request with Temperature 0, TopP 0.9 and StopSequences ["X"]
   - setup: one request with none of them
   ```
   assert b1.options.temperature==0 && 'temperature' in b1.options; assert 'temperature' not in b2.options; assert none(k in b for k in ['keep_alive','format','images'])
   ```

### REQ-3: Tools and tool choice

**Rationale:** Ollama's tool type carries only a subset of JSON Schema and has no tool-choice field.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE ollama provider SHALL declare each core.ToolWire, in request order, as a function tool with its name, its description and the tool-schema subset obtained by JSON-encoding its InputSchema and decoding it into the SDK's tool-parameter type
   → a schema with additionalProperties, format and minimum records a tool whose parameters keep type, properties, required, enum, items and descriptions but none of those three keywords
   Check: integration
   - setup: two tools; the first schema has additionalProperties:false, a string property with format "uri", an integer with minimum 1, an enum, an array with items, descriptions and required
   ```
   p=b.tools[0].function.parameters; assert p.required==[...]; assert !contains(json(p),'additionalProperties'|'format'|'minimum')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a core.ToolWire has a nil InputSchema, THE ollama provider SHALL declare the tool with an empty object schema
   → recorded parameters equal {"type":"object","properties":{}}
   Check: unit
   - setup: a ToolWire with InputSchema nil
   ```
   assert json_equal(b.tools[0].function.parameters, {type:'object',properties:{}})
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF a tool's schema cannot be decoded into the SDK's tool-parameter type, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL fail the turn before any HTTP request is sent
   → the stream ends with a non-nil Err whose text starts with "ollama:" and names the tool; the recording server sees zero requests
   Check: unit
   - setup: a tool "bad_tool" whose schema encodes to JSON the SDK parameter type rejects (e.g. a property type of an incompatible JSON shape)
   - setup: a recording server
   ```
   res = drain(c.Stream(ctx, req)); assert res.Err != nil; assert hasPrefix(res.Err.Error(),'ollama:') && contains(...,'bad_tool'); assert srv.count==0
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN Request.ToolChoice is core.ToolChoiceNone, THE ollama provider SHALL send no tools key at all, while ToolChoiceUnset and ToolChoiceAuto send the declared tools
   → the recorded body has no "tools" key under ToolChoiceNone
   Check: unit
   - setup: a request with one tool
   ```
   assert 'tools' not in bodyNone; assert len(bodyUnset.tools)==1 && len(bodyAuto.tools)==1
   ```

### REQ-4: Transcript replay

**Rationale:** The second turn of a tool loop must pair results to calls by id and keep the arguments the server sent.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE ollama provider SHALL pass Request.Messages through provider.RepairToolPairing before encoding, never mutate the caller's slice, and send the repair report to Options.Warnf when the repair changed anything (discarding it when Warnf is nil)
   → Warnf is called exactly once when the repair changed the transcript and not at all otherwise; the input messages are deeply equal before and after Stream
   Check: unit
   - setup: a transcript with an assistant tool call that has no result
   - setup: a clean transcript
   - setup: a Warnf spy
   - setup: a deep copy of the first transcript
   - setup: a second client with Warnf nil
   ```
   drain(stream(broken)); assert warn.calls==1; assert reflect.DeepEqual(broken, copy); assert contains(body,'No result provided')
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] THE ollama provider SHALL send a core.UserMessage as role user with its text as content, and a core.AssistantMessage as role assistant with its text as content and one tool_calls entry per ToolUseBlock carrying the block's id, its position among the message's calls as index, its name and arguments decoded from ToolUseBlock.Input
   → recorded assistant message carries tool_calls[i].id equal to the block ID and function.index equal to i
   Check: integration
   - setup: a transcript: user text; assistant with text and two ToolUseBlocks (ids call_a, call_b); a successful result for call_a; an error result for call_b
   ```
   a=b.messages[1]; assert a.tool_calls[1].id=='call_b' && a.tool_calls[1].function.index==1; t=b.messages[3]; assert t.role=='tool' && t.tool_call_id=='call_b' && startsWith(t.content,'Error: ')
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE ollama provider SHALL for any JSON object in ToolUseBlock.Input, replay its arguments with their keys in the order of those bytes
   → the recorded arguments' key order equals the key order of Input
   Check: property
   - setup: an assistant message whose single ToolUseBlock has generated Input
   ```
   for obj in gen_ordered_objects(): body = record(withInput(obj.bytes)); assert keyOrder(rawArguments(body)) == obj.keys
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] THE ollama provider SHALL set the assistant message's thinking to the concatenated text of its non-redacted thinking blocks only when the message's Model equals m.ID, and drop all other thinking without sending it as content
   → thinking from another model or a redacted block appears nowhere in the recorded body
   Check: unit
   - setup: an assistant message with Model == m.ID carrying a thinking block "mine1", a redacted block "redacted-secret" and another thinking block "mine2"
   - setup: an assistant message with Model "other-model" carrying thinking "foreign-thought"
   ```
   assert b.messages[1].thinking=='mine1mine2'; assert !contains(raw,'redacted-secret') && !contains(raw,'foreign-thought')
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] THE ollama provider SHALL send each core.ToolResultMessage, in transcript order, as one tool message whose content is provider.ToolResultText of the result, with the tool's name and the tool-call id it answers
   → recorded tool message carries role "tool", tool_name, tool_call_id and content prefixed "Error: " when IsError is true
   Check: same as REQ-4.2

### REQ-5: Effort as think

**Rationale:** The catalog row decides which think levels a model accepts, read the same way provider/anthropic reads it, with no clamping.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the request's effort is empty or m.ThinkingKind is core.ThinkingKindNone, THE ollama provider SHALL send no think field
   → the recorded body has no "think" key
   Check: unit
   - setup: a request with empty effort on a model with efforts
   - setup: a request with effort high on a model whose ThinkingKind is none
   ```
   assert 'think' not in b1 && 'think' not in b2
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN the request carries a non-empty effort and m.Efforts is nil, THE ollama provider SHALL send think as the effort's own name as a string level
   → effort high on an unlisted model records "think":"high"
   Check: unit
   - setup: an unlisted model with Efforts nil
   ```
   assert b.think == 'high'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN the request carries a non-empty effort and m.Efforts is non-nil, THE ollama provider SHALL send no think when the effort is absent from the map or maps to nil, and otherwise send the mapped value trimmed and lower-cased as a string level, never substituting another level
   → xhigh on the qwen3.8:27b row records no "think"; medium records "think":"medium"
   Check: unit
   - setup: the qwen3.8:27b row from catalog.Select("ollama","STANDARD","")
   - setup: a custom map {medium: " Medium ", low: nil}
   ```
   assert 'think' not in rec('xhigh'); assert rec('medium').think=='medium'
   ```

### REQ-6: Streaming decode

**Rationale:** The loop consumes canonical events and a final message regardless of vendor.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN the first chunk of a response arrives, THE ollama provider SHALL push MessageStartEvent with a partial message whose Model is m.ID, whose Effort is the request's effort and whose Timestamp comes from Options.Now
   → the first event is core.MessageStartEvent with those three fields set
   Check: unit
   - setup: Options.Now returning a fixed time T
   - setup: request effort medium
   ```
   e := events[0].(core.MessageStartEvent); assert e.Message.Model==m.ID && e.Message.Effort=='medium' && e.Message.Timestamp==T
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN a chunk carries non-empty message.thinking or message.content, THE ollama provider SHALL stream thinking as ThinkingStartEvent and ThinkingDeltaEvent and content as TextStartEvent and TextDeltaEvent, close the open block when the kind switches, append each completed block to the partial message followed by a MessageUpdateEvent, and never report thinking as text
   → the final message holds a ThinkingBlock and a TextBlock in streamed order; no TextDeltaEvent carries thinking text
   Check: unit
   - setup: a server streaming thinking "ponder" in two chunks, then content "answer" in two chunks, then a done chunk
   ```
   assert kinds(final.Content)==['thinking','text']; assert all(!contains(d.Delta,'ponder') for d in textDeltas)
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN a chunk carries tool calls, THE ollama provider SHALL turn each call into one ToolUseBlock built through core.NewToolUse that keeps the vendor's id and whose Input is the arguments' JSON with keys in wire order (absent arguments become {}), pushing ToolCallStartEvent then one ToolInputDeltaEvent carrying the whole argument JSON before appending the block
   → the final message's ToolUseBlock.ID equals the wire id and Input preserves the server's key order
   Check: unit
   - setup: a server chunk with a tool call id "call_9", name "lookup" and arguments {"zeta":1,"alpha":2,"mid":3}
   - setup: a second call with no arguments
   ```
   assert final.tool[0].ID=='call_9'; assert keyOrder(final.tool[0].Input)==['zeta','alpha','mid']; assert final.tool[1].Input=='{}'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] THE ollama provider SHALL for any set of tool calls without an id across one or more responses of one Client, synthesize ids that are unique within each response and across responses
   → no two ToolUseBlock IDs produced by the same Client are equal
   Check: property
   - setup: one Client against a server that serves tool calls without ids
   ```
   seen=set(); for resp in gen_responses(): for b in toolBlocks(stream(resp)): assert b.ID != '' and b.ID not in seen; seen.add(b.ID)
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] WHEN the done chunk arrives, THE ollama provider SHALL after processing its own content, push TextEndEvent, ThinkingEndEvent and ToolCallEndEvent in block order, build the final message with RawStopReason equal to done_reason verbatim, ResponseModel equal to the chunk's model and Usage per 28-REQ-8, push MessageEndEvent and end the stream
   → the stream result's Message is the final message and Err is nil
   Check: unit
   - setup: servers streaming: (a) text, tool call, done_reason "stop"; (b) text, tool call, done_reason "length"; (c) text only, done_reason "stop"; model "resp-model" in the done chunk
   ```
   assert endOrder==blockOrder; assert (a).StopReason==ToolUse; assert (b).StopReason==Length; assert (a).RawStopReason=='stop'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.6] THE ollama provider SHALL set StopReason to StopReasonLength when done_reason is length (even with tool calls), otherwise to StopReasonToolUse when the message has tool calls, otherwise to StopReasonStop
   → done_reason "stop" with a tool call yields core.StopReasonToolUse
   Check: same as REQ-6.5
1. [REQ-6.7] WHILE several goroutines call Stream on the same *Client concurrently, THE ollama provider SHALL complete every stream independently with no data race
   → each stream yields its own final message; go test -race reports no race
   Check: unit
   - setup: one Client
   - setup: a server echoing a per-request marker into its response text
   - setup: go test -race
   ```
   parallel(32, i -> assert text(drain(c.Stream(ctx, reqWith(i)))) == marker(i))
   ```

### REQ-7: Incomplete turns and errors

**Rationale:** A local server's failures are not transient, so each one is named once, without retries, and a partial turn can never run a tool.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] IF Stream is called with a context that is already done, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL return the context's error without sending a request, and carry every later failure inside the stream as the failed message followed by Err on the last item
   → (nil channel, ctx.Err()); the recording server sees zero requests
   Check: unit
   - setup: a cancelled context
   - setup: a recording server
   ```
   ch, err := c.Stream(cancelledCtx, req); assert ch==nil && err==context.Canceled; assert srv.count==0
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF the stream ends, or the SDK Chat call returns, without a done chunk, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL end the turn with StopReasonError and a terminal ErrorEvent, keeping the text and thinking that streamed and dropping every tool call
   → Err wraps ollama.ErrStreamTruncated; the message has no ToolUseBlock
   Check: unit
   - setup: a server that streams text "partial" and a tool call, then closes the body without done:true
   ```
   assert errors.Is(res.Err, ErrStreamTruncated); assert msg.StopReason==Error; assert noToolUse(msg); assert lastError.Terminal
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] IF the caller's context is cancelled while a request is in flight, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL stop the request within 1 second and end the turn with StopReasonAborted and ErrorMessage "Request was aborted", pushing no ErrorEvent and keeping no tool call, taking precedence over every other error classification
   → Err is core.ErrAborted; the message has no ToolUseBlock
   Check: integration
   - setup: a server that sends a text chunk and a tool call chunk, then blocks
   ```
   cancel(); res = waitWithin(1s); assert res.Err==core.ErrAborted; assert msg.ErrorMessage=='Request was aborted'; assert noErrorEvent && noToolUse(msg)
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] IF connecting to the host fails (refused, DNS failure or no route), THEN THE ollama provider SHALL end the turn with an error naming the host, suggesting ollama serve and naming OLLAMA_HOST
   → Err wraps ollama.ErrUnreachable; text starts with "ollama:"
   Check: integration
   - setup: a provider whose Host is a loopback port that was listened on and closed
   ```
   assert errors.Is(res.Err, ErrUnreachable); assert contains(txt,host) && contains(txt,'ollama serve') && contains(txt,'OLLAMA_HOST')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] IF the server answers 404, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL end the turn with an error naming the model and the host, including Ollama's message and suggesting ollama pull <model>
   → Err wraps ollama.ErrModelNotFound and errors.As yields *ollama.StatusError with Code 404
   Check: integration
   - setup: a server answering 404 with {"error":"model 'qwen3.8:27b' not found"}
   ```
   var se *StatusError; assert errors.Is(err, ErrModelNotFound) && errors.As(err,&se) && se.Code==404; assert contains(txt,'ollama pull '+m.ID)
   ```
1. [REQ-7.6] IF Ollama's error message, in a status error or an error line inside a 200 stream, says the input exceeds the context length, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL end the turn with an error naming the model and the num_ctx sent, including Ollama's message and saying that a model already loaded at a smaller length keeps it until it unloads
   → Err wraps ollama.ErrContextWindow
   Check: integration
   - setup: a server answering 400 with {"error":"the input length exceeds the context length"}
   - setup: another server answering 200 with an error line of the same message in the stream
   ```
   for srv in [status400, inStream]: assert errors.Is(err, ErrContextWindow); assert contains(txt,'32768') && contains(txt,m.ID) && contains(txt,'unloads')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.7] IF the server answers any other non-2xx status or sends any other error line inside a 200 stream, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL end the turn with StopReasonError and a terminal ErrorEvent; for 401 or 403 the text names the host, says AgentKit sends no credential to Ollama and says to check OLLAMA_HOST; for other statuses the text is "ollama: HTTP <code>: <Ollama's message>"; an in-stream error carries Ollama's message classified by the rules of 28-REQ-7.4 to 28-REQ-7.6
   → Err is a *ollama.StatusError{Code, Text} for a status error; a non-nil error starting with "ollama:" for an in-stream error
   Check: integration
   - setup: servers answering 401, 403, 500 {"error":"boom"}, and 200 with an in-stream error line {"error":"model runner crashed"}
   ```
   assert se.Code==401 && contains(txt,'no credential') && contains(txt,'OLLAMA_HOST'); assert txt500=='ollama: HTTP 500: boom'
   ```
1. [REQ-7.8] THE ollama provider SHALL make exactly one HTTP attempt per Stream call, and start every error text with "ollama:" while never including the value of any environment variable other than OLLAMA_HOST in an error, event or warning
   → the recording server counts exactly one request per Stream call for every failure status
   Check: integration
   - setup: servers answering 404, 401, 429, 500, 503 and a closed port
   - setup: distinctive values set for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OLLAMA_API_KEY
   - setup: a Warnf spy
   ```
   for st in statuses: drain(stream()); assert srv.count==1; assert hasPrefix(err,'ollama:'); assert !containsAny(allText, secrets)
   ```

### REQ-8: Usage and zero cost

**Rationale:** Ollama runs on the embedder's hardware, so a run is priced at zero rather than flagged unpriced.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN the done chunk reports usage, THE ollama provider SHALL set InputTokens to prompt_eval_count minus prompt_eval_cached_count floored at 0, CacheReadTokens to the cached count only when it is positive, OutputTokens to eval_count, Requests to 1 and the cost to 0 with its presence bit, leaving reasoning tokens unset, for listed and unlisted model ids alike
   → 354/256/120 yields core.Usage{InputTokens: 98, CacheReadTokens: 256, OutputTokens: 120, Requests: 1, CostUSD: 0} with Has(core.UsageCostUSD) true
   Check: unit
   - setup: a done chunk with prompt_eval_count 354, prompt_eval_cached_count 256, eval_count 120
   - setup: once with a listed model id and once with an unlisted one
   ```
   u := final.Usage; assert u.InputTokens==98 && u.CacheReadTokens==256 && u.OutputTokens==120 && u.Requests==1; assert u.Has(UsageCostUSD) && u.CostUSD==0
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] THE ollama provider SHALL for any non-negative prompt, cached and eval counts, report InputTokens = max(0, prompt - cached), report OutputTokens = eval and report CacheReadTokens only when cached > 0
   → InputTokens is never negative
   Check: property
   - setup: done chunks with generated counts
   ```
   for p,c,e in gen(): u=usageOf(done(p,c,e)); assert u.InputTokens==max(0,p-c) && u.OutputTokens==e; assert u.Has(CacheRead)==(c>0)
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] IF a turn fails before its done chunk, THEN THE ollama provider SHALL report Requests 1 and no token fields
   → the failed message's Usage has Requests 1 and no input, output or cache-read presence bits
   Check: unit
   - setup: a server that answers 500
   - setup: a server that truncates the stream
   ```
   u := msg.Usage; assert u.Requests==1 && !u.Has(Input) && !u.Has(Output) && !u.Has(CacheRead)
   ```

### REQ-9: Dependency pin and policy

**Rationale:** A new third-party module enters the root module only as a deliberate, pinned and approved change that leaves every existing test meaning the same.

1. [REQ-9.1] THE dependency policy tests SHALL require github.com/ollama/ollama as a direct, non-indirect requirement of the root module at exactly v0.40.7, listed in approvedDeps with a reason comment and in preSpec13Direct

1. [REQ-9.2] THE dependency policy tests SHALL compare the root and sandbox module graphs to regenerated snapshots (go-list-m-all.txt, sandbox-go-list-m-all.txt and sandbox-go-list-m-all.14.txt), recording every version raised by minimum version selection as an accepted upgrade in a map distinct from d1Upgrades and deleting no test
   → TS-13-65, TS-14-42, TS-15-40 and TS-17-60 pass with the restated expectations
   Check: integration

   - setup: an accepted-upgrades map distinct from d1Upgrades

1. [REQ-9.3] THE repository layout tests SHALL expect the provider directories anthropic, faux, ollama and openrouter in TestProviderDefaults_TS09_11

   Check: unit

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent completes a two-turn tool loop on a recording Ollama server

1. **embedder** builds the provider with ollama.New(catalog.Select("ollama", "STANDARD", "") row, Options{Env: {"OLLAMA_HOST": <recording server>}}) and passes it as agentkit.Config.Provider with one tool
2. **agent loop** calls Stream with the system prompt, the user message, the tool and effort medium
3. **ollama provider** encodes model qwen3.8:27b, num_ctx 32768, truncate false, think medium, stream true and the tool-schema subset, and sends one /api/chat request with no Authorization header
4. **recording server** streams thinking, a tool call with an id and ordered arguments, and a done chunk with done_reason stop
5. **ollama provider** decodes the chunks into events and a final message with StopReasonToolUse and zero-cost usage
6. **agent loop** runs the tool and calls Stream again with the transcript
7. **ollama provider** replays the tool-call id, ordered arguments, thinking text and the paired tool result with the tool's name in the second request
8. **recording server** streams a final text and a done chunk
9. **agent loop** ends the run with the final text and a total cost of 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** agentkit.Agent loop, ollama provider, ollama api client, catalog.Select, provider.RepairToolPairing, core, httptest server

**Setup:**

- a recording server streaming turn 1: thinking, tool call id "call_1" with arguments in order {"zeta":..,"alpha":..}, done_reason stop with 354/256/120 counts; turn 2: final text and done
- provider built with ollama.New(catalog.Select("ollama","STANDARD","") row, Options{Env:{OLLAMA_HOST: server}})
- an agent with one tool whose schema has additionalProperties and effort medium
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OLLAMA_API_KEY set

**End state:**

- two requests are recorded, both with model qwen3.8:27b, num_ctx 32768, truncate false, think "medium", stream true and the tool with the schema subset
- neither request has an Authorization header or any env secret
- the second request carries id call_1, arguments in server key order, a tool message with tool_name and tool_call_id call_1, and the first turn's thinking on the assistant message
- the run ends with the final text and total cost 0
- the tool handler ran exactly once

**Pseudocode:**

```
res = agent.Run(ctx,'go'); assert len(srv.reqs)==2; assert second.messages has assistant{tool_calls[0].id=='call_1', thinking} and tool{tool_call_id:'call_1'}; assert res.Usage.CostUSD==0
```

### PATH-2: An agent run on an unavailable model or server ends with a named error

1. **embedder** builds the provider against a recording server that answers 404 (or against a closed port) and runs the agent
2. **ollama provider** sends exactly one /api/chat request attempt
3. **ollama provider** ends the turn with StopReasonError, a terminal ErrorEvent and an error wrapping ErrModelNotFound naming ollama pull <model> (or ErrUnreachable naming ollama serve)
4. **agent loop** returns the run error to the embedder without running any tool

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** agentkit.Agent loop, ollama provider, ollama api client, net/http, httptest server

**Setup:**

- a recording server answering 404
- a second provider pointed at a closed port
- an agent with a tool whose handler records invocations

**End state:**

- the server records exactly one request
- the 404 run's error wraps ollama.ErrModelNotFound and names "ollama pull <model>"
- the closed-port run's error wraps ollama.ErrUnreachable and names "ollama serve"
- the final message has StopReasonError and the tool handler never ran

**Pseudocode:**

```
err = agent.Run(ctx,'go'); assert errors.Is(err, ErrModelNotFound); assert srv.count==1; assert handler.calls==0
```

### PATH-3: A stream cut before its done chunk ends the run without executing a partial tool call

1. **embedder** runs the agent against a recording server that streams text and a tool call, then closes the body without done:true
2. **ollama provider** ends the turn with ErrStreamTruncated, keeping the streamed text and dropping the tool call
3. **agent loop** short-circuits the turn and returns the error to the embedder with the tool handler never invoked

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** agentkit.Agent loop, ollama provider, ollama api client, httptest server

**Setup:**

- a recording server that streams text and a tool call then closes the body without done:true
- an agent with a tool whose handler records invocations

**End state:**

- the run returns an error wrapping ollama.ErrStreamTruncated
- the assistant message keeps the streamed text and carries no tool call
- the tool handler was never invoked

**Pseudocode:**

```
err = agent.Run(ctx,'go'); assert errors.Is(err, ErrStreamTruncated); assert handler.calls==0
```

|--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| `NewClient` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `func NewClient(base *url.URL, http *http.Client) *Client` | Used instead of ClientFromEnvironment, which reads the process environment. |
| `Client.Chat` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `func (c *Client) Chat(ctx context.Context, req *ChatRequest, fn ChatResponseFunc) error` | Calls fn once per streamed line; returns nil at end of body even without done:true; returns StatusError for status >= 400; returns a plain error for an in-stream {"error":...} line. |
| `ChatResponseFunc` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `type ChatResponseFunc func(ChatResponse) error` |  |
| `ChatRequest` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `type ChatRequest struct{ Model string; Messages []Message; Stream *bool; Tools Tools; Options map[string]any; Think *ThinkValue; Truncate *bool }` | Truncate per the 2026-10-21 probe. |
| `ThinkValue` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `type ThinkValue struct{ Value any }` | Marshalled as a bool or a string level. |

| `Tool` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `type Tool struct{ Type string; Function ToolFunction }; type ToolFunction struct{ Name, Description string; Parameters ToolFunctionParameters }` | Parameters decodable from JSON Schema keeping type, description, enum, items, properties and required. |
| `ChatResponse` | `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` | `type ChatResponse struct{ Model string; Message Message; Done bool; DoneReason string; Metrics }; type Metrics struct{ PromptEvalCount, PromptEvalCachedCount, EvalCount int; ... }` | PromptEvalCachedCount per the probe. |

- 7.2 Implement fail(text, err) like anthropic's decodeState.fail: an abort gives StopReasonAborted, ErrorMessage "Request was aborted", Err core.ErrAborted and no ErrorEvent; any other failure gives StopReasonError, a terminal ErrorEvent, then MessageEndEvent; use the caller's context (not the derived one) to detect cancellation, which takes precedence over every other classification; cancel must stop the request within 1 second
- 7.3 A Chat return or stream end without a done chunk ends with an error wrapping ErrStreamTruncated; the failed message keeps streamed text and thinking and drops every tool call (also on abort)
- 7.4 Classify errors from client.Chat: net.OpError/dial failure wraps ErrUnreachable (names host, `ollama serve`, OLLAMA_HOST); api.StatusError 404 wraps ErrModelNotFound and also yields *ollama.StatusError{Code:404} via errors.As (names model, host, Ollama's message, `ollama pull <model>`)
- 7.5 Recognise a message saying the input exceeds the context length (status error or in-stream error) as ErrContextWindow: text names the model and the num_ctx sent, includes Ollama's message and says a model already loaded at a smaller length keeps it until it unloads
- 7.6 401/403 give a *StatusError text naming the host, saying AgentKit sends no credential to Ollama and to check OLLAMA_HOST; other statuses give *StatusError{Code, Text: "ollama: HTTP <code>: <message>"}; an in-stream error line becomes an "ollama:"-prefixed error with Ollama's message classified by the same rules
- 7.7 Make exactly one HTTP attempt per Stream call (no retries); every error text starts with "ollama:" and never includes any environment variable value other than the host
- 7.8 A failed turn's Usage has Requests 1 and no input, output or cache-read presence bits
- 7.9 Run `go test ./provider/ollama/... -race -count=1`
